telangana_a.name: Telangana
telangana_a.scope: Irrigated rice-based systems in Telangana and peninsular India. The reference farm's second season is tentative.

rows.check: Paddy rice seasonal ET · Hyderabad trial
rows.interpretation: Span of eight irrigation treatments, from alternate wetting and drying to continuous flooding. Published ET covers 100 days after transplanting, a different basis from the catalog's full crop window. Inclusion describes the trial span.
rows.locator: Table 2, p. 119 (seasonal ET); p. 118 (variety duration and irrigation regimes)

rows.check: Paddy rice seasonal ET · Sangareddy estimate
rows.interpretation: District-scale CROPWAT crop demand. A point comparison gives the difference from this estimate without a dispersion measure.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, Table 3 in the manuscript; totals agree with the journal abstract, pp. 1047–1052

rows.check: Green gram seasonal ET · Sangareddy estimate
rows.interpretation: Regional potential crop demand. The paper does not measure a green gram crop after paddy on the demo farm.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, Table 3 in the manuscript; totals agree with the journal abstract, pp. 1047–1052

rows.check: Chickpea (Bengal gram) seasonal ET · Sangareddy estimate
rows.interpretation: Regional potential crop demand for the study's Bengal gram season. Crop durations, rainfall and irrigation can vary.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, Table 3 in the manuscript; totals agree with the journal abstract, pp. 1047–1052

rows.check: Difference in seasonal ET · paddy minus green gram
rows.interpretation: Both put crop ET higher for paddy. This contrast reuses the two Sangareddy crop estimates and says nothing about farm irrigation savings.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, Table 3 in the manuscript; totals agree with the journal abstract, pp. 1047–1052

rows.check: Field water applied and percolation · Jagtial
rows.reference: 1,276.5 mm applied, 402.86 mm crop ET, 452.13 mm percolation
rows.interpretation: The technology note provides component observations but gives no cultivar or crop-window details. These show how gross water applied can diverge from crop ET. They cannot constrain the rotation's water withdrawal or supply fraction.

rows.check: Paddy rice variety duration · Hyderabad
rows.reference: 120 to 125 days
rows.interpretation: Reported duration of MTU-1010. The field ET calculation covers only the post-transplant part. This comparison informs the crop window input.
rows.locator: Table 2, p. 119 (seasonal ET); p. 118 (variety duration and irrigation regimes)

rows.check: Green gram before paddy · N credit
rows.reference: 29–36 kg N/ha in material used as green manure. Rice mean 6.39 t/ha versus 4.70 after fallow.
rows.interpretation: Rice yield moved in the direction expected from a benefit. Incorporated biomass N is a different quantity from N fertilizer replaced. The trial does not isolate a successor fertilizer-equivalent response for the model's harvested grain legume.

rows.check: Cowpea before paddy · N credit
rows.reference: 38–50 kg N/ha in material used as green manure. Rice mean 6.34 t/ha versus 4.70 after fallow.
rows.interpretation: Positive rice yield response under incorporation. The mass of N returned includes N taken up from soil and gives no estimate of crop-available or fertilizer-equivalent N.

rows.check: Paddy before green gram · residual nutrient effect
rows.reference: Green gram seed yield 8.56% lower following normal transplanting than after dry direct-seeded rice. Uptake varied with rice establishment and manure form.
rows.interpretation: The study contrasts paddy management and manure treatments. The scorer has one paddy credit and no management-specific nutrient carryover.

rows.check: Harvested cowpea with haulms incorporated before rice · Coimbatore
rows.reference: 49–52 kg N/ha in the haulms. First rice yielded 4.80 and 4.45 t/ha versus 4.35 and 4.28 in the control sequence.
rows.interpretation: The table reports sequence means pooled across N rates separately from fertilizer means. The trial shows first-crop response with incorporation, but the table lacks the paired rate-specific yields required to infer a fertilizer-equivalent credit.

rows.check: Summer green gram before rice · Pilicode
rows.reference: Following-rice yields 4.48–4.67 t/ha across green gram treatments versus 4.46 t/ha after summer fallow. Treatment yield differences were not statistically significant.
rows.interpretation: The N rates varied for the preceding pulse. The following rice yields do not provide a fertilizer response curve for the successor. A nonsignificant yield result does not establish a zero credit.
rows.locator: Materials and Methods §3 and Table 18, pp. 13–15, 54–55

kenya_makueni_north.name: Makueni
kenya_makueni_north.scope: Maize–bean systems in semi-arid eastern Kenya, including Machakos and Makueni. Cropland at the demo coordinate is unverified.

rows.check: Common bean before sole maize · N credit
rows.reference: 44 to 80 kg N/ha
rows.interpretation: Fertilizer equivalents of 80 in the 1982 long rains and 44 in 1982/83 short rains. The 80 comparison follows the season order assumed at the demo farm. Both agree with a positive credit. Yield response can include effects besides N and two seasons do not establish a modern field credit.

rows.check: Cowpea before sole maize · N credit
rows.reference: 12.5 to 24 kg N/ha
rows.interpretation: Fertilizer equivalents of 12.5 in long rains and 24 in short rains. The catalog lies within this two-season span, above the long-rains estimate. This is a crop-specific comparison.

rows.check: Maize–bean rotation and bean residues · residual mineral N
rows.reference: Rotation plots had higher residual mineral N than continuous maize at Masii and lower at Kimutwa.
rows.interpretation: The reprinted abstract shows site-dependent residual effects. It does not expose the treatment tables needed to attribute a fertilizer-equivalent range to one residue regime and crop sequence.
rows.locator: Abstract of the Kimutwa and Masii maize–bean field study, pp. 172–173

rows.check: Maize seasonal ET · Katumani and Makindu budgets
rows.reference: 335 to 355 mm
rows.interpretation: Table 1 uses cultivar medians of 335 mm for Makindu and 355 mm for Katumani in both rainy seasons. The comparison uses published water-budget inputs. Maximum crop demand was not measured in this study.

rows.check: Common bean seasonal ET · Katumani short rains
rows.interpretation: Coefficient-based seasonal requirement for an approximately 80-day dry bean crop. This endpoint is distinct from measured water use under rainfall stress.

rows.check: Common bean actual water use · rainfed and irrigated
rows.reference: 187–245 mm rainfed and 481–503 mm fully irrigated
rows.interpretation: Treatment water use reflects soil storage, rainfall, supplemental water and a short-season cultivar. Pooling irrigation regimes would give a misleading reference range for one nominal ET input.

rows.check: Soil-water carryover and simultaneous crop competition
rows.model: Seasonal bucket starts empty. One crop per slot.
rows.reference: Sole crops had higher near-surface moisture than the intercrop at 4 and 8 weeks after planting in 2019 short rains.
rows.interpretation: Observations are within a season in the top 20 cm. The trial does not estimate planting-time water carryover between the model's two crop slots.

rows.check: Common bean maturity · Katumani short rains
rows.reference: 69 to 78 days
rows.interpretation: Short-season KAT X56 physiological maturity. The catalog window is longer and may include time from maturity to harvest.

rows.check: Early maize maturity · Machakos
rows.reference: 100 to 125 days
rows.interpretation: Study's locally grown early-maturity group. The extra-early group is reported at 90–110 days and is distinct from the main comparison.

rows.check: Seasonal grain yields and intercropping · Katumani
rows.model: Binary thermal and rainfall suitability per crop window. One crop per slot.
rows.reference: Maize sole vs intercrop 2.88 vs 3.21 t/ha in 2019 short rains and 0.97 vs 1.08 in 2020 long rains. Beans 0.44–1.64 t/ha in contrasting 2019 treatments, with crop failure in 2020 long rains.
rows.interpretation: Cropping system effect on maize grain yield was significant in the short-rains trial and not significant in the long-rains trial. Bean treatment extremes also differ in tillage and fertilizer. These trials provide neither a climate cut-off nor a yield comparison for the demo rotation.

rows.check: Rainfed bean grain yield across short rains
rows.reference: 1,107 and 978 kg/ha in 2012/13 and 2013/14 at 156 and 259 mm in-crop rainfall, respectively.
rows.interpretation: Both trials produced grain. Grain was observed under a relatively dry crop window, which cautions against reading the model threshold as a crop failure boundary. The study supplies no comparable minimum-rainfall curve.

rows.check: Sequential versus simultaneous maize–bean systems · Katumani
rows.model: Unitless per-crop income index. No within-slot mixed crops.
rows.reference: Three-season production value 10,500 KSh/ha for sole-crop rotation, 6,585 for continuous intercrop and 5,198 for continuous sole maize.
rows.interpretation: Table VI values output at historical prices. The model's income index has no calibrated conversion to trial gross or net returns.

mote.name: Mote et al. (2018), Journal of Agrometeorology
mote.locator: Table 2, p. 119 (seasonal ET); p. 118 (variety duration and irrigation regimes)
mote.design: Replicated lowland rice irrigation trial, Rajendranagar, 2013–2014.

kumar.name: Kumar et al. (2022), International Journal of Environment and Climate Change
kumar.locator: Section 3.3, Table 3 in the manuscript; totals agree with the journal abstract, pp. 1047–1052
kumar.design: CROPWAT crop ET estimates for Sangareddy. Published modeled point values give no trial spread.

surekha.name: Surekha et al. (2013), The Andhra Agricultural Journal
surekha.design: Five crop years on a Hyderabad Vertisol. Pre-kharif legumes and incorporation were compared with fallow.

pjtau.name: PJTSAU, Agro Technologies 2020–21
pjtau.design: University extension water budgeting in Northern Telangana, with crop ET and deep percolation recorded separately.

vineela.name: Vineela et al. (2026), Legume Research
vineela.design: Tirupati field trial on how rice establishment and organic nutrient management affect the following green gram.

nadar.name: Nadar and Faught (1984), East African Agricultural and Forestry Journal
nadar.design: Katumani trials with sole-crop rotations and intercrops. Fertilizer equivalence was inferred from a continuous-maize fertilizer response curve.

musingi.name: J. B. Kioko Musingi (1990), University of Nairobi MSc thesis
musingi.design: Katumani 1988/89 short rains. Pan evaporation and crop coefficients from one field-season calculation for two dry bean varieties.

recha.name: Recha et al. (2016), Arid Land Research and Management
recha.design: Seasonal rainfed maize water budgets for Katumani and Makindu using assumed cultivar median ET and station rainfall.

sennhenn.name: Sennhenn et al. (2017), Frontiers in Plant Science
sennhenn.design: Katumani short-rains field trials in 2012/13 and 2013/14 with rainfed and irrigation treatments.

wafula.name: Wafula et al. (2022), Tropical and Subtropical Agroecosystems
wafula.design: Katumani plots in the 2019 short and 2020 long rains, with tillage, fertilizer and crop arrangement treatments.

ndegwa.name: Ndegwa et al. (2022), Weather, Climate, and Society
ndegwa.design: Machakos county weather-index study with a description of early and extra-early maize varieties. Duration only here.

kenya_abstract.name: Kenya Soil Health Consortium, Soil Fertility Management Book of Abstracts
kenya_abstract.locator: Abstract of the Kimutwa and Masii maize–bean field study, pp. 172–173
kenya_abstract.design: Accessible reprint of the study abstract. Underlying treatment tables could not be read.

palaniappan.name: Palaniappan and Siddeswaran (1994), SARP Research Proceedings
palaniappan.design: Two Coimbatore cycles with grain harvest followed by haulm incorporation. The lowland rice trial crossed crop sequences with fertilizer rates.

adarsh.name: Adarsh (2019), Kerala Agricultural University MSc thesis
adarsh.locator: Materials and Methods §3 and Table 18, pp. 13–15, 54–55
adarsh.design: Pilicode trial with four summer pulses and a fallow control in double-cropped lowland rice. The design varies N for the summer pulse.
